question: Should OpenClaw add a native ASR/STT backend abstraction now, and should the first implementation slice be macOS Push-to-Talk with a reusable provider/security contract?
rationale: The feature gap is source-reproducible, but the safe implementation crosses native app capture, Gateway/provider ownership, new settings/config, credential isolation, private-network policy, and fallback UX.

options.title: Start With macOS PTT
options.body: Preserve platform speech by default, implement the narrower macOS Push-to-Talk seam first, and make the provider/security contract reusable for later native surfaces.

options.title: Design Broad Cross-Platform ASR
options.body: Scope macOS, iOS, Android, and possibly WebChat settings together, accepting larger design and validation risk up front.

options.title: Defer Native ASR Core Work
options.body: Keep self-hosted STT on existing media, Talk relay, channel, plugin, or sidecar paths until maintainers prioritize a native-app extension point.

recommendation.title: Start With macOS PTT
recommendation.body: Preserve platform speech by default, implement the narrower macOS Push-to-Talk seam first, and make the provider/security contract reusable for later native surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The recommended first slice is native macOS PTT/Talk, and steipete has the strongest recent history across that surface and adjacent Talk handoff behavior.
